S4SD00049.name: Mike Rounds
S4SD00049.bio: U.S. Senator from South Dakota since 2014; former two-term Governor of South Dakota, state senator and business owner.

positions.stance: Stands with the America First agenda and will "fight for and support policies that put South Dakota and America FIRST!"
As a Senate Armed Services Committee member, working to make sure the U.S. military "remains the best in the world."
Believes in local control of education; says a "one size fits all" federal directive does not serve children well.
"A strong supporter of the Second Amendment" who works to protect the rights of law-abiding gun owners.
Supports an "all-of-the-above" approach to energy production and maximizing U.S. natural resources to lower costs and reduce reliance on foreign energy.

S4AK00214.name: Dan S. Sullivan
S4AK00214.bio: U.S. Senator from Alaska since 2015 and retired U.S. Marine Corps Reserve colonel; former Alaska Attorney General and Commissioner of the Alaska Department of Natural Resources.

positions.stance: Says Alaskans are "being crushed by skyrocketing costs" and pledges to fight to make life affordable for Alaska families.
Wants to get special interests out of politics, hold Congress accountable, and proposes congressional term limits.
Pledges "practical, Alaska-first solutions to restore our fisheries," citing harm from out-of-state factory trawlers.
Will fight to invest in Alaska energy production to create good-paying jobs and "bring down energy costs."
Will fight to ensure Alaska veterans receive "the healthcare, benefits, and pay they’ve earned."

S6AK00326.name: Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.
S6AK00326.bio: Former U.S. Forest Service forestry worker and elementary school teacher who has also worked in logging, construction, steel mills and bartending.

S6WY00217.name: James Byrd
S6WY00217.bio: Former member of the Wyoming legislature with a background in business leadership and public service.

positions.stance: Will fight to lower energy costs by supporting responsible domestic production, cutting red tape, and ending "wasteful foreign wars"; opposes food-industry consolidation.
Opposes efforts to sell off or privatize public lands and wants them kept open for hunting, fishing, grazing, and recreation.
Will push to lower prescription drug costs, protect rural hospitals from closure, and make insurance work for the people paying into it.
Skeptical of data centers in Wyoming; won't support "sweetheart tax deals" or projects that strain the grid and water supplies.
Supports honest country-of-origin labeling and pushes back on regulatory overreach that burdens family ranching operations.

S6WY00209.name: Harriet Hageman
S6WY00209.bio: U.S. Representative for Wyoming; describes herself as a fourth-generation Wyomingite.

S4TX00888.name: Ted Brown
S4TX00888.bio: Retired self-employed independent insurance adjuster and longtime Libertarian Party official, including former chairman of the Libertarian Party of California.

positions.stance: Opposes government-mandated age verification, digital ID requirements, internet censorship, and limits on VPNs, citing privacy and surveillance concerns.
"Repeal the income tax, abolish the IRS, and replace them with nothing"; pledges never to vote to raise taxes.
"Audit the Federal Reserve as a first step, then end it," and legalize competing currencies.
Supports an "Ellis Island-style" system with free movement of people, ending checkpoints and raids, and abolishing ICE.
Supports non-intervention: bring all troops home, end foreign military interventions, withdraw from NATO, and end foreign aid.

S6FL00863.name: Neil J. Gillespie
S6FL00863.bio: Founder and director of Justice Network and former licensed motor vehicle dealer in Pennsylvania.

positions.stance: Top priority: "Restore integrity in our government through the separation of powers doctrine."
Prioritizes First Amendment protections, including free speech and press, separation of church and state, assembly, and the right to petition.
Believes immigration laws must be enforced and ICE "must be reined in when its conduct becomes excessive, inhumane, or unaccountable."
Supports school choice, school board accountability, fairer K-12 funding for lower-resource communities, and strong national academic benchmarks.
Supports voter ID, early in-person voting, and requested absentee ballots; opposes universal mail-in voting.
Believes violent criminals "should be prosecuted firmly" and policing must respect constitutional rights and remain accountable to communities.
"I am pro-life"; believes the law should protect unborn life in all circumstances and supports more maternal health care.
"Lower costs, simpler taxes, and an end to wasteful spending."
"Fight inflation and protect savings from hidden taxation."
"Remove barriers so entrepreneurs and workers can thrive."
Supports "local control, skills training, and parent empowerment."
"More choice, transparency, and patient-first solutions."

S6NC00563.name: Michael Dublin
S6NC00563.bio: Recently retired public school teacher, community activist and veteran who has led a prison ministry for over two decades.

positions.stance: Wants to overturn Citizens United, pass campaign finance reform, and end gerrymandering and voter suppression.
Supports "a Green New Deal for North Carolina" with renewable energy, union jobs, and accountability for corporate polluters.
Supports criminal justice reform, ending mass incarceration, protecting voting rights, affordable housing, and quality education in every zip code.
Favors "diplomacy over endless war" and reducing the military budget to reinvest in schools, hospitals, and communities.
Supports defending the Second Amendment "with responsible ownership and safety measures."
Will push to end remaining Patriot Act provisions for sneak-and-peek warrants and National Security Letters.
Opposes warrantless surveillance and license plate reader networks; proposes a Bill of Digital Rights making personal data your property.
Wants to repeal the 100-mile inland zone allowing warrantless searches, keeping inspection "at the actual border."
Supports ending qualified immunity so people can hold government accountable when their rights are violated.
Will advocate for a $1,000 monthly Universal Basic Income for citizens over 18, and $1,500 for descendants of chattel slavery.
Supports a single-payer system so every U.S. citizen has access to quality health services by default.
Says private equity should not own residential property, rents should be tied to prevailing wages, and short-term rentals regulated.
Calls for ceasing hostilities against Iran and pursuing permanent ceasefires in Gaza, Ukraine, and elsewhere.
Demands justice for Flint, accountability for PFAS contamination, and stopping Line 5 and the Line 5 tunnel.

S0NJ00258.name: Veronica Fernandez
S0NJ00258.bio: Co-owner of a small commercial electrical contracting business and former licensed property/casualty insurance underwriter.

positions.stance: Will sign on to a proposed 28th Amendment resolution to overturn Citizens United "on day one."
"I am a FIERCE supporter of M4A" and will sign on to Medicare for All legislation immediately.
Calls to abolish ICE immediately and replace it with "a vigorous and fast-tracked path to citizenship."
Cannot support any government with a hierarchy of citizenship by religion or race; condemns Hamas and atrocities against Palestinians.
Supports open primaries for all registered voters and independent commissions to draw state and congressional district lines.

S8MA00268.name: Shiva Ayyadurai
S8MA00268.bio: Founder and CEO of CytoSolve, Inc., who has started several technology companies including EchoMail and Systems Health.

positions.stance: "End censorship, protect medical freedom, and return science to the people."
"Rip lobbyists and billionaires out of government" so resources go to working people.
Shift from "sick-care" to preventive and integrative medicine, nutrition, and systems biology.
Cut taxes for families and small business and "End the Fed’s inflation robbery."
"Ban poisons in food and agriculture, enforce honest labeling."

S6MA00288.name: Joe Tache
S6MA00288.bio: Youth worker, community organizer, and socialist based in Boston.

positions.stance: Proposes seizing the top 100 corporations as public property and a 100% tax on assets above $10 million to fund housing, healthcare, and education.
Proposes a National Climate Emergency Act to seize and decommission fossil fuel infrastructure and build a renewable energy grid.
Through a National Employment Emergency Act, would "guarantee well-paid union jobs and job training."
Supports cutting the military budget by 90% and calls to "Free Palestine and end the billionaires’ war drive."
Calls to "stop scapegoating immigrants, Black America, women, and the LGBTQ community," opposing what it calls a right-wing assault on rights.

wiki:andrew-gerena.name: Andrew Gerena
wiki:andrew-gerena.bio: Has worked in military service, security, commercial trucking, information technology, food service, maintenance, and scientific research.

positions.stance: "Re-direct federal funding from the War Budget towards Education, Infrastructure, Research, and Job training programs."
"Cut off Military Aid to any countries suspected of war crimes."
"Fix the corrupt, profit based healthcare system."
"Common sense budgeting, rejecting any Tax increase."
"Investigate AIPAC for Espionage and Treason against the United States."
"Defend our US_Constitution, Clarify our History, and Restore Equality for Humans."
"Provide team support as we undo the recent acts of insurrection."
Lists "Protection of American Human Freedom" as a campaign priority.
Proposes "Activation of US_Fort Knox" with $3.3 trillion for legislation and a $33 trillion debt resolution "to provide relief for Americans."
Lists "Drafting of Equal Earnings Act" as a campaign priority.

S6TN00372.name: Robert Jones
S6TN00372.bio: Small business owner and executive director of a nonprofit in Jonesborough, Tennessee.

positions.stance: Will seek to pass an Accountability Act creating a secure system for public servants to survey constituents on key issues.
Will not accept campaign donations, asking supporters to give to local nonprofits instead; "Money will not buy my support."
Calls for community-based solutions on food costs, affordable prefabricated housing, rethinking the healthcare system, and public safety.
Says policy should prioritize "steady growth, rational decision-making, and long-term stability," with predictable, moderate inflation.
Will advocate for equitable treatment of workers, "wages that represent your value," and improved work-life balance.

S6TN00364.name: Yoshi Matthews
S6TN00364.bio: Founder of FTP Nonprofit with a background in business, accounting, nonprofit service, and community outreach.

positions.stance: Proposes "a narrowly defined, Tennessee-based solution that is fair, lawful, and limited in scope" for a specific historic injustice.
"No Tennessee senior should lose their home to property taxes after a lifetime of work and contribution."
Proposes a universal basic income to provide "a reliable financial foundation for eligible Americans."
"Lower the cost of living, support working families and small businesses, and promote responsible economic growth."
"Secure the border, enforce immigration laws, and support a functional legal immigration system."
Focuses on "practical solutions that reduce everyday costs" for groceries, housing, and fuel.
Running as an independent with "no blind loyalty to Democrats or Republicans."
Will push for term limits and more transparency in spending, and hold elected officials to performance standards.
Calls for "policies shaped by lived experience" and a "focus on opportunity, not bureaucracy."
Supports constitutional rights, "balanced, responsible governance," and respect for the rule of law.

S6TN00414.name: Catherine Whitson
S6TN00414.bio: Former insurance industry professional who has spent 20 years volunteering as a life coach, pastor and mentor.

positions.stance: Lowering costs, creating high-paying jobs, supporting small businesses, and promoting green energy, safe water, and recycling.
Work to reduce prescription drug costs, protect rural hospitals, and support veterans, seniors, and those in need.
Boost public school funding, expand vocational training, support private and home schooling, and find ways to pay off student debt.
Affordable housing for all and tiny house communities for unhoused Tennesseans through partnerships with churches and businesses.
Promote better childcare, eldercare, and assistance so "all people have the opportunity to live their best life."
